Order 
This petition under Section 528 of BNSS has been filed by the petitioners being aggrieved by the order dated 13.02.2026 passed by II Additional Sessions Judge, Ganj Basoda, District Vidisha in S.T. No.80/2023, whereby the application under Section 311 of Cr.P.C./Section 348 of BNSS filed by the petitioners has been rejected.

entities.text: II Additional Sessions Judge, Ganj Basoda
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2 . As per the prosecution story, on 12/07/2023, information was received at Police Station Shamshabad, District Vidisha that Priyanka Yadav W/o Vijay Pal Yadav (Petitioner No.1) had consumed poison.
The present petitioners along with another person took Priyanka to the hospital.
Thereafter, petitioner No.2 informed the complainant and his family members about the incident.
Subsequently, the statement of Priyanka was recorded, wherein she alleged that her husband had administered something to her and he intended to remarry.

During the course of treatment,
Priyanka NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:6739 2 MCRC-8680-2026 succumbed.
Thereafter, a merg was registered and statements of the deceased's family members were recorded.
In their statements, it was alleged that the petitioners were harassing the deceased in connection with a demand for dowry.

It was further alleged that the petitioners had demanded Rs.15,00,000/-
and were subjecting the deceased to harassment in relation to the said demand.

3. Upon completion of the investigation, a charge sheet was filed and charges under Sections 304B and 498A of the IPC along with Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act were framed against the petitioners.
After framing of charges, the trial commenced and witnesses were examined.
Thereafter, on 04/02/2026, an order was passed closing the right of defence and the matter was listed for final hearing on 11/02/2026.

On 11/02/2026, the Trial Court upon perusal of the record Vijay Pal Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/26097698/
1 altered the charges against the petitioners and an alternate charge under Section 302 IPC was framed against petitioner No.1 and charges under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC were framed against petitioners No.2 and 3.

entities.text: Vijay Pal Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said order, directions were also issued to both the prosecution and the defence to clarify their stand within two days with respect to re-examination of witnesses.

4 . Pursuant to the said directions, the petitioners filed an application under Section 217 Cr.P.C.
seeking recall of witnesses for re-examination.
However, the Trial Court without properly appreciating the provisions of law partly dismissed the application.
Only certain selected witnesses were permitted to be re-examined while recall of other material witnesses was denied without assigning any cogent reasons.

Being aggrieved by the said NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:6739 3 MCRC-8680-2026 order, the petitioners have preferred the present petition.

5 . Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that Trial Court erred in not considering the provisions of law as initially the charges were framed against the petitioners under Sections 304B,
498A of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Thereafter, by invoking the provisions of Section 216 of Cr.P.C. Trial Court had altered the charge under Section 302 of IPC against the petitioners.
Trial Court while rejecting the application filed by the petitioners has not given any cogent reasoning while dismissing the application under Section 217 of the Cr.P.C.
Denial of the opportunity to cross-examine the witnesses after alteration of charges may result in a grave miscarriage of justice.

Learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the judgment passed by the Supreme Court in the case of R. Rachaiah Vs. Home Secretary, Bangalore reported in (2016) 12 SCC 172 in support of his submission.

entities.text: R. Rachaiah Vs. Home Secretary, Bangalore reported in (2016) 12 SCC 172
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, this petition may be allowed and opportunity of cross examination of witnesses after alteration of charge may be given to the petitioners.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents appended thereto.
7.

In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that after alteration of the charge by adding Section 302 of the IPC, the petitioners were entitled to a fair and adequate opportunity to cross-examine the material witnesses in light of the modified charge.
The right of cross-examination is a valuable and substantive right, forming an integral part of a fair trial.

Since the right of the petitioners to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:6739 4 MCRC-8680-2026 effectively cross-examine the witnesses stood closed despite alteration of the charge to one under Section 302 IPC, which carries graver consequences, such closure has resulted in serious prejudice to the defence.

8. Accordingly, the impugned order dated 13.02.2026 to the extent it denies the petitioners a full opportunity to recall and cross-examine the twenty three material witnesses after alteration of charge, cannot be sustained and is hereby set aside.
The petition is allowed and the Trial Court is directed to afford the petitioners an adequate opportunity to recall and cross-examine the said twenty three material witnesses in accordance with law.
9. The petition stands disposed of in above terms.
